text: The year was 1889, and the last natural forest on Earth was a spectacle that many traveled miles to behold. Eli, a young botanist, stood in awe among the ancient trees, a leather-bound journal in hand as he recorded notes about species that had become legends. This sacred grove, unbeknownst to him, was about to become the centerpiece of a historic preservation effort that would challenge the industrial metropolis encroaching upon the natural world. The city, located in France, was rapidly transforming, with the iron lattice of the Eiffel Tower rising in the distance, symbolizing the relentless march of progress that threatened to swallow the last remnants of the wild.
